title: Responsive Safety in Reinforcement Learning by PID Lagrangian Methods
authors: Adam Stooke, Joshua Achiam, Pieter Abbeel
venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR vol. 119
conclusions: Traditional Lagrangian methods for constrained (safe) RL update the multiplier by pure integral control, which produces oscillations and cost overshoot/violations during training.
The paper reinterprets the Lagrange multiplier update as a control-theory problem and adds proportional and derivative terms (PID control) to the standard integral-only update.
Proportional control (PI-control) damps oscillations and improves robustness to the integral learning rate K_I across multiple Safety Gym environments (DoggoGoal, DoggoButton, CarButton, PointGoal).
Derivative control further prevents cost overshoot and slows the approach to the constraint boundary, acting predictively rather than reactively.
A complementary reward/cost scale-invariance technique (beta-weighting of the policy gradient) makes controller tuning transferable across differently-scaled reward/cost objectives.
CPPO (PID-Lagrangian applied to PPO) sets a new state of the art on the Safety Gym benchmark, improving the return-vs-constraint-violation Pareto frontier over the plain Lagrangian baseline.
